name: Daal Chawal
description: Comforting Pakistani daal chawal with tender lentils, fluffy basmati rice and a fragrant garlic-cumin tarka for an everyday home-style meal.
ingredients: 1 cup moong or masoor lentils, rinsed
2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20–30 minutes
method: Put the rinsed lentils in a pot with turmeric, salt and about 3 cups water. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer and cook until tender, adding hot water in small amounts only when needed.
Add the chopped tomato once the lentils are tender and simmer until it softens into the daal. Adjust with hot water to keep the consistency pourable rather than excessively thick.
For the rice, bring plenty of salted water to a boil. Drain the soaked basmati, add it to the boiling water and cook until tender while the grains still hold their shape, then drain immediately.
Let the drained rice rest covered for a few minutes so excess steam settles, then fluff gently without crushing the grains.
For the tarka, heat the ghee or oil and fry the cumin, sliced garlic and onion until aromatic and golden. Add the red chilli powder only briefly at the end so it does not burn.
Carefully pour the hot tarka over the daal, stir lightly, taste for salt and serve immediately with the warm rice, achar and salad.
tips: Lentils thicken as they stand, so keep a little hot water available to adjust consistency.
Do not burn the garlic or chili in the tarka; both can turn bitter.
storage: Cool leftover rice and daal promptly and refrigerate them in covered containers. Reheat the portion you plan to serve until thoroughly hot.
